data.narrative:
Meter is a Series C–stage company in the Housing & Construction sector founded by Anil and Sunil Varanasi. The company has raised $305M to date. The comparable universe is limited: one private peer (ICON) and no public comps, reflecting the early-stage and specialized nature of the frontier-tech subsector.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($305M) as a proxy for enterprise value and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement yields an implied valuation of $518M. This reflects the expected value accretion between Series C and the subsequent financing or exit event, normalized across similar-stage companies in adjacent sectors.

The triangulated valuation range is $441M (low) to $596M (high), with $518M as the central estimate. However, this analysis carries material uncertainty. The single-method approach relies entirely on stage-progression heuristics without revenue, profitability, or market-size anchors. The comp set comprises only one private peer with no public reference points, limiting cross-validation. Key variables—customer concentration, unit economics, and path to profitability—remain unobserved. Any valuation within the $441M–$596M band should be treated as indicative pending disclosure of financial performance and market-size assumptions.
